text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz unveiled a national agriculture programme yesterday by saying it must pave the way for talks on accession to EU.

- The cabinet Thursday decided to set aside HUF 1.4 billion to partially compensate the needy for the recent energy price hikes. The cabinet agreed to spend HUF 300 billion over the next seven years to build 121 km of motorway and 184 km of "half motorways".
- The budget deficit for the first two months of the year was some 33 percent lower than expected, according to Finance Ministry data.

- A World Bank delegation and representatives of the Agriciulture Ministry, the Finance Ministry and the National Bank of Hungary held negotiations yesterday on a possible World Bank loan for agricultural financing.
- Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea devoted the second day of his visit here to promoting stronger economic ties and actively encouraging Hungarian investment into his country.
- Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima is due to visit Budapest today.

- Farmers in Kunszallas blocked construction of the M5 motorway saying they will prevent the further construction until they receive equitable indemnification for their land appropriated for the project.
- A total of HUF 9.5 billion is available for economic development from the Industry, Trade and Tourism Ministry this year, said deputy state secretary Lajos Berenyi.
- The Hungarian Insurance Companies Association issued an appeal against the State Insurance Supervision's decision to grant a license to the life insurer Grawe Rt.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- A police spokesman said thousands of policemen and plainclothes detectives will be mobilised to maintain law and order at March 15 commemoration events in Budapest today and tomorrow. Gyorgy Ekrem Kemal, leader of an extremist right-wing group is in police custody after large quantities of weaponry were found in his apartment.
- Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus will pay a one-day official visit to Budapest on Monday.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn yesterday declined to accept the resignation of Zoltan Kis, political state secretary at the Agriculture Ministry.
- The number of foreigners legally finding jobs in Hungary is slowly declining, according to data.

- The car manufacturer Suzuki Rt. will appeal the HUF 30 million fine imposed Wednesday by the Economic Competition Office. Frigyes Banki, deputy managing director of Suzuki said that the company has amended those contracts featuring fixed prices.
- Investors have subscribed all 622,000 Gardenia shares, prompting the underwriters to close the issue yesterday, ahead of the originally scheduled March 21.
- The telecommunications equipment companies Ericsson Tavkozlesi Kft and Ericsson Business Communications Rt. will merge on May 1.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Domestic investors had subscribed the whole HUF 6.44 million package of Mezogep shares by the end of the second day of subscription.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Commercial Employees Union issued a statement yesterday against the Polus Centre and Duna Plaza stores for being open on the March 15 national holiday.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
